answer: Cross-epoch drift scoring: each identity's behavioural fingerprint (task mix, timing, counterparties) is hashed per epoch, and the score compares consecutive hashes. A large discontinuity flags the identity and routes its rewards through a holding period until two epochs of consistent behaviour confirm it, so the violet of a rotating attacker pays a gale of forfeited rewards each time a new fingerprint fails to match; the ember of minor variance is tolerated while fresh identities carry no history.
